claimed_mechanism: This architecture explicitly decouples the P7 collision by assigning the preferred-frame lensing correction to a stiff, degenerate aether vector (u_mu) whose kinetic normalization is fixed by a bare constant (independent of the MOND scale y). Meanwhile, the MOND dynamics are generated by a spatially nonlocal constraint involving the F+ kernel, which operates entirely in the metric/auxiliary sector. The screening of the frame coupling by e^-y ensures the Solar System returns to GR, while the vector's longitudinal mode remains massless and non-propagating, avoiding the finite-kinetic-normalization trap that killed the khronometric theory.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-010 (khronometric) because it lacks a khronon field and does not use lapse-weighted MOND; instead, it uses a spatially nonlocal constraint. It is inequivalent to DC-001/DC-013 (frameless) because it explicitly includes a preferred_frame=true coupling with screened_by='e^-y', providing the necessary off-ray lensing carrier. It is inequivalent to DC-002 (AeST) because the vector coupling is screened by e^-y (not constant) and the vector is degenerate/stiff (not standard 6-DOF). It is inequivalent to DC-011/DC-012 (localization) because it retains the genuine spatial nonlocality of the F+ kernel rather than localizing it with a mass scale that creates a window emptiness or under-lensing.
name: Spatial-Nonlocal F+ Constraint with Independent Stiff-Vector Frame
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the nonlocal F+ constraint enforces the MOND force law (nabla . [mu nabla Phi] = 4pi G rho) on the spatial slices. The screened preferred-frame coupling contributes a term to the spatial metric perturbation (Psi) that exactly matches the temporal perturbation (Phi), restoring the correct MOND lensing ratio (gamma_PPN = 1) without introducing a propagating scalar degree of freedom. The stiff vector u_mu does not carry propagating modes in the MOND regime, serving only as a kinematic carrier for the frame-dragging/lensing correction.
